No prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or executable package code was found in the skill content.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Always lint after changes** - Run `markdownlint --fix` then `markdownlint` to verify
2. **Run from repository root** - Ensures `.markdownlint.json` config is loaded
The project uses markdownlint with these specific rules (from `.markdownlint.json`):
- **MD003**: Heading style must be ATX (`# Heading` not `Heading\n===`)
- Use ATX style (`#`) not underline style
Use the `process_order()` method to handle orders.
The `$order_id` parameter must be an integer.
- Most markdown issues are auto-fixable with `markdownlint --fix`

content.value_statement: WooCommerce documentation needs consistent Markdown that passes project lint rules. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical rules for headings, lists, links, tables, code blocks, and lint checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains WooCommerce markdownlint rules for headings, list indentation, code fences, and file endings.
Provides examples for headings, ordered lists, unordered lists, links, tables, directory trees, and emphasis.
Gives a workflow for auto-fixing and checking Markdown from the repository root.
Shows fixes for common markdownlint errors including MD007, MD031, MD032, MD036, and MD040.
Covers README, changelog, and CLAUDE.md formatting expectations for WooCommerce documentation.
limitations: Does not install markdownlint or configure project tooling.
Does not validate Markdown unless the assistant runs the recommended checks.
Focused on WooCommerce conventions, not every Markdown style guide.
Does not replace human review for technical accuracy.

use_cases.title: Prepare WooCommerce README Files
use_cases.description: Create README sections with clear headings, scannable lists, and code block labels that match project rules.

use_cases.title: Fix Markdown Lint Failures
use_cases.description: Resolve common lint issues such as list indentation, missing blank lines, and unlabeled code fences.

use_cases.title: Standardize Assistant Documentation
use_cases.description: Review CLAUDE.md files for structure, hierarchy, and formatting that remains easy for AI tools to parse.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Formatting
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single Markdown file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WooCommerce Markdown file for heading levels, list spacing, link style, and code fence languages. Suggest concise fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Lint Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply project rules after markdownlint reports problems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the selected Markdown to follow WooCommerce markdownlint rules. Preserve meaning and call out any manual follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite A README Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a documentation section before review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this README section using WooCommerce Markdown conventions. Add clear headings, scannable lists, and language labels for code blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Documentation Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across multiple documentation files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these documentation changes as a WooCommerce maintainer. Identify style drift, repeated headings, broken structure, and checks to run.

output_examples.input: A README section has skipped heading levels, mixed list markers, and unlabeled examples.
output: Moves headings into a clear hierarchy.
Uses one unordered list marker consistently.
Adds language labels to examples that need them.

output_examples.input: A markdownlint report flags list indentation and missing blank lines around blocks.
output: Adjusts nested lists to the WooCommerce indentation style.
Adds blank lines around block content while preserving meaning.

output_examples.input: A CLAUDE.md file needs review before being added to the WooCommerce repository.
output: Checks that the structure is easy for AI tools to parse.
Improves headings and table of contents placement.
Notes any remaining content questions for maintainers.

best_practices: Run the project Markdown check from the repository root after edits.
Use one top-level heading and maintain heading order.
Add language names to every fenced code block.
anti_patterns: Do not use bold text as a substitute for headings.
Do not mix unordered list markers in one file.
Do not leave plain code fences without a language label.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create and edit WooCommerce Markdown files that follow project documentation and linting conventions.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it modify files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an assistant can apply when editing Markdown files.

faq.question: Does it cover non-WooCommerce projects?
faq.answer: It may be useful elsewhere, but its rules are tailored to WooCommerce documentation standards.

faq.question: How should I verify the output?
faq.answer: Run the repository Markdown lint check and review the content for technical accuracy.

faq.question: Can it help with CLAUDE.md files?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for clear, structured assistant documentation files.
